en.name: Tapioca pearls, dry
en.summary: Uncooked tapioca pearls keep about 12 months sealed in a dry cupboard, both from purchase and after the bag is opened. They are cassava starch and nothing else, so what ends them is damp: a pearl that has picked up moisture goes hard in the middle and will never cook through.
en.pantry: A sealed bag in a cool, dry, dark cupboard is all they ask for, and about 12 months is a reasonable working life — take that as guidance borrowed from plain dry tapioca rather than as a figure anyone has published for 生粉圓. Reseal tightly every time: damp pearls fuse into a solid lump, and once they have taken up moisture they can mould. Age shows itself as a texture failure long before it becomes a safety one — old pearls harden and craze, and no amount of boiling will bring them back to a proper chew. Keep them away from the hob and off a damp floor.
en.fridge: There is no reason to refrigerate dry pearls and a good reason not to. A fridge is humid, and every time the bag comes out it collects condensation, which is exactly what turns loose pearls into a brick. Keep them in the cupboard instead. Cooked pearls are a completely different food — a wet cooked starch that belongs in the fridge and has a life measured in a day or so, not months.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for dry tapioca pearls and freezing them is not worth doing. The problem the freezer would solve is time, and time is not what kills them; moisture is, and the freezer is a source of it. If you have bought a catering sack, split it into small airtight jars and keep them in the cupboard rather than putting the lot in the freezer.
spoilage: Pearls fused into a single hard lump in the bag.
Musty smell, or visible mould on pearls that have taken up damp.
Surface crazing and cracks; the pearls stay chalky in the centre after boiling.
Insects, webbing or fine starch dust suggesting weevils.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar rather than relying on the original bag.
Write the opening date on the jar; pearls age by hardening, not by smelling bad.
Buy the small bag — a kitchen rarely gets through a catering sack in a year.
Boil what you will drink today; cooked pearls do not keep.

faq.q: How long do uncooked tapioca pearls last?
faq.a: About 12 months sealed in a dry cupboard, before and after opening. Keep the bag sealed: damp pearls go hard in the middle and never cook through.

faq.q: Do dry tapioca pearls need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No, and it is better not to. The fridge is humid and condensation makes the pearls clump.

faq.q: Why do my pearls stay hard in the middle?
faq.a: They are old. Dry pearls harden and crack with age and never cook through properly again. It is a texture failure, not a safety problem.

zh.name: 生粉圓
zh.summary: 未煮的粉圓密封放乾燥櫥櫃，從購買日起算、以及開封之後，都大約是 12 個月。它就只是樹薯澱粉，所以終結它的是受潮：吸了濕氣的粉圓煮起來中心會硬，怎麼煮都煮不透。
zh.pantry: 密封袋放陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃就夠了，大約 12 個月是合理的期限——請把這個數字理解成向乾燥木薯粉粒借來的參考，而不是誰為「生粉圓」發表過的規定。每次用完都要確實封緊：受潮的粉圓會黏成一整塊，一旦吸了水氣就可能發霉。年紀大的粉圓在變得不安全之前，會先在口感上壞掉——它會變硬、表面龜裂，再怎麼煮都煮不出應有的 Q 度。請遠離爐台，也不要放在潮濕的地面。
zh.fridge: 生粉圓沒有理由冷藏，而且有明確理由不要。冰箱潮濕，袋子每拿出來一次就結一次露水，那正是把鬆散粉圓變成一塊磚的原因。放櫥櫃就好。煮熟的珍珠則是完全不同的食物：那是含水的熟澱粉，該放冰箱，而且能放的時間以一天上下計算，不是幾個月。
zh.freezer: 生粉圓沒有公布的冷凍期限，也不值得冷凍。冷凍能解決的是時間，但殺死粉圓的不是時間而是水分，而冷凍庫正是水分的來源。如果買了營業用大包，請分裝成小的密封罐放櫥櫃，而不是整包丟冷凍。
spoilage: 袋子裡黏結成一整塊硬塊。
有霉味，或受潮的粉圓表面看得到霉點。
表面龜裂有紋，煮完中心還是白心、粉粉的。
有蟲、絲網，或袋底出現細澱粉粉末。
tips: 倒進密封罐保存，不要只靠原本的塑膠袋。
在罐子上寫開封日期，粉圓老化是靠變硬、不是靠發臭表現的。
買小包就好，一般家庭一年很難用完營業用大包。
今天要喝多少就煮多少，煮好的珍珠放不住。

faq.a: 密封放乾燥櫥櫃，開封前後大約都是 12 個月。袋子一定要封好：受潮的粉圓中心會硬，怎麼煮都煮不透。
不需要，而且最好不要。冰箱潮濕，結露會讓粉圓黏成一塊。

faq.q: 為什麼我的珍珠煮不透、中間還是硬的？
faq.a: 它太老了。放久的粉圓會變硬、龜裂，之後怎麼煮都煮不透。這是口感問題，不是安全問題。
